newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders says USDA data bearish soy, grains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders says USDA data bearish soy, grains.

text.p: CBOT traders said monthly supply/demand data issued by USDA were bearish for soybean, wheat and corn futures.
Soybeans were called to open down five to seven cents a bushel on the data, with corn and wheat expected to open off one to three cents.
USDA left its soybean ending stocks estimate for 1996/97 unchanged at 125 million bushels and its corn ending stocks estimate for 1996/97 unchanged at 909 million.
"It (the report) is bearish on corn and beans as they left ending stocks unchanged," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities in Iowa.

Many analysts had been expecting soybeans ending stocks to be cut by five million to 10 million bushels due to a strong U.S. crush pace and export demand. Some analysts were also looking for a cut in corn ending stocks of up to 40 million bushels although views were more mixed than on soybeans.
